records.title: Prairie School house
records.designPeriod: Prairie School influence, c. 1890s–1920s; contemporary original interpretation
records.eraRationale: The exact original source uses a horizontal house composition, low roof, broad eaves and Roman-brick emphasis.
records.canadianContext: Compare Canadian domestic landscape relationships while keeping Prairie School distinct from the Canadian geographic Prairies.
records.internationalContext: The movement’s early 20th-century Midwestern US context is an international teaching connection.

records.title: Postmodern neighbourhood library
records.designPeriod: Postmodern influence, c. 1960s–1990s; contemporary original interpretation
records.eraRationale: The original library uses a strongly marked entrance, historical references, contrasting forms and colour.
records.canadianContext: Compare late 20th-century civic identity, context and communication with current community facilities.
records.internationalContext: Postmodernism is an architectural movement, not proof of a participatory planning process.

records.title: Bauhaus-inspired design workshop
records.designPeriod: Bauhaus influence, 1919–1933; later Canadian postwar Modernist connections
records.eraRationale: The original glazed workshop references functional volumes and visible making spaces; no historic building is reconstructed.
records.canadianContext: Connect interwar European ideas with Canadian postwar uptake of Modernist architecture.
records.internationalContext: The source references Bauhaus-related architecture, not a measured reconstruction of Dessau.

records.title: De Stijl artist studio
records.designPeriod: De Stijl influence, 1910s–1930s; contemporary original interpretation
records.eraRationale: The studio’s interlocking planes and limited primary-colour palette reference the Dutch interwar movement.
records.canadianContext: Use this international example to compare architectural composition with Canadian contemporary infill.
records.internationalContext: The movement’s Dutch origin remains explicit; colourful planes do not establish a neighbourhood planning ideology.

records.title: Mughal-inspired reading pavilion
records.designPeriod: Mughal-inspired reference, broadly 16th–18th centuries; contemporary original interpretation
records.eraRationale: The pavilion’s cusped arcade, dome, shade and ordered composition reference a historical South Asian design family.
records.canadianContext: Use it as an international comparison for shelter, public space and garden relationships in Canadian urban design.
records.internationalContext: Mughal is one South Asian historical influence, not all South Asian or Islamic architecture.
